# Cookie without Secure or HttpOnly (Go)

`qualor:go/insecure-cookie` · Security hotspot · Severity: Low · [CWE-614](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/614.html), [CWE-1004](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1004.html) · OWASP Top 10: [A02:2025 Security Misconfiguration](https://top10.owasp.org/2025/A02_2025-Security_Misconfiguration/), [A05:2021 Security Misconfiguration](https://top10.owasp.org/2021/A05_2021-Security_Misconfiguration/)

> **Security hotspot.** This rule asks for a review: it marks code that is often safe and
> sometimes not, and a person decides which. A hotspot never fails the quality gate.

## What it finds

<!-- begin: what-it-finds -->
Cookies set without the `Secure` flag, without the `HttpOnly` flag, or without both:

- an `http.Cookie` handed to `http.SetCookie` (also through Echo's `c.SetCookie`) whose `Secure`
  or `HttpOnly` field is missing or `false`, built in the call, in a variable, or by a helper
  function of the same file that returns the cookie (`http.SetCookie(w, newSessionCookie(token))`);
- Gin's `c.SetCookie(name, value, maxAge, path, domain, secure, httpOnly)` with `secure` or
  `httpOnly` set to `false`.

Cookies that are being deleted (`MaxAge: -1`, or an expiry at the Unix epoch) are not reported.
<!-- end: what-it-finds -->

## Why it matters

<!-- begin: why-it-matters -->
Without `Secure`, the browser also sends the cookie over plain HTTP, where anyone on the network
path can read it. Without `HttpOnly`, every script on the page can read it, including a script
injected through a cross-site scripting flaw. For a session id or a token, either gap is enough to
take over the user's session.

Not every cookie holds a secret: a language preference or a UI setting may well go without these
flags. That is why this is a hotspot: check what the cookie holds.
<!-- end: why-it-matters -->

## Example

<!-- begin: example -->
**Noncompliant:** a session cookie without `Secure` and `HttpOnly`.

```go
package session

import "net/http"

func Login(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	token := newSessionToken()
	http.SetCookie(w, &http.Cookie{Name: "session", Value: token, Path: "/"})
}

func newSessionToken() string { return "generated" }
```

**Compliant:** both flags set (and `SameSite`, which limits cross-site requests).

```go
package session

import "net/http"

func Login(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	token := newSessionToken()
	http.SetCookie(w, &http.Cookie{
		Name:     "session",
		Value:    token,
		Path:     "/",
		Secure:   true,
		HttpOnly: true,
		SameSite: http.SameSiteLaxMode,
	})
}

func newSessionToken() string { return "generated" }
```
<!-- end: example -->

## How to fix

<!-- begin: how-to-fix -->
- For a session id, a token or other sensitive data, set both flags: `Secure: true, HttpOnly: true`
  on the `http.Cookie`, or `secure` and `httpOnly` `true` in Gin's `SetCookie`.
- Consider `SameSite: http.SameSiteLaxMode` (or `Strict`) as well.
- If the cookie holds nothing sensitive and scripts must read it, the code can stay as it is.
<!-- end: how-to-fix -->

## Frameworks and APIs covered

- `net/http`
- Gin
- Echo

## Known limits

<!-- begin: known-limits -->
- Cookies built by a function of another file or package, by a helper that fills a variable
  before returning it or returns the cookie together with an error, or passed in as a parameter,
  and `Set-Cookie` headers written by hand, are not checked.
- Flags set on a variable after the literal are tracked only roughly: reusing one variable for a
  second cookie, setting a flag between two calls, setting it inside a closure, or assigning
  `false` later can hide an unsafe cookie.
- Flags set by a helper function (`harden(c)`) are not seen, so such a cookie is reported.
- Cookie helpers are recognised by name: if two types in the file have methods of the same name
  and one of them leaves a flag out, calls of the other are reported too.
- A cookie deleted with another negative `MaxAge` than `-1`, or with an expiry in the past other
  than the epoch, is reported.
<!-- end: known-limits -->

## Tests

The test file [`rules/go/cookie/insecure-cookie.go`](../../../rules/go/cookie/insecure-cookie.go) holds every case the rule reports or accepts:
lines marked `ruleid:` must be reported and lines marked `ok:` must not. The known limits are
marked `todoruleid:` (missed) and `todook:` (wrongly reported). `npm test` runs them with OpenGrep,
and checks the example above as well.
